Name: Michelle Corbin
Badge: Everyday Sparks 2.0
Which strategy from this module (Daily Schedule, Take a Line for a Walk or Interpreting Visual Texts) feels most immediately usable in your teaching context? Why?:

Interpreting Visual Texts feels like the one most immediately usable in my classroom right now. Students are naturally drawn to visuals- myself included- and I believe pictures help generate and spark new ideas and thinking since kids can "see" what is happening - or at least what they think is happening - and they don't have to rely solely on their imagination or prior knowledge. I love using the Ouisi cards I was given during the Fall meeting. More importantly, the kids LOVE them, too. Descriptive writing has blossomed, and the kids are begging to write!

What other strategies or approaches have you used to engage your students in routine writing over the course of this school year? What, if any, challenges have you encountered in engaging students in sustained routine writing?:
I have to admit that the online program "We Will Write" has changed some things about writing that have been happening in my classroom. In the beginning of the year, I relied heavily on writing strategies that I had learned at the summer conference. After time went on, the students seemed to be getting bored of the routines, although I was asking more and more from them as writers. I believe I was first introduced to "We Will Write" while at the summer event with Literacy That Works (by another teacher in one of my discussion groups), and the name popped up again at some point on a middle school ELA platform online. I gave it a try, and my kids were hooked! Once again, I was getting writing out of them that I couldn't believe. It was a great way to introduce each type of writing we would be doing throughout the school year.
